findings.asked: Features of a homologous series, the series with general formula CnH2n, the formula of a 12-carbon alkane, the definition of a hydrocarbon, and the products of burning methane.
findings.wentWrong: CnH2n was not recognised as the alkenes; the alkane formula was sometimes left as C12H24+2; 'hydrocarbon' definitions dropped the word 'only' or called the atoms molecules; combustion products were given as names when formulae were required.
findings.rule: Alkanes CnH2n+2, alkenes CnH2n; a hydrocarbon contains hydrogen and carbon ONLY; CO2 and H2O as formulae.

findings.asked: Hydrocarbon definition, complete-combustion products, and the balanced equation for incomplete combustion of methane.
findings.wentWrong: The definition again lost 'only' (or called the atoms ions); incomplete combustion equations were partly right, with formula marks but not the balance.
findings.rule: Incomplete combustion gives carbon monoxide (and/or carbon) and water; balance the oxygen last.

findings.asked: Identify compounds from structures: which are gases, which is an alkane, name a four-carbon alkene, draw butane, write a word equation for its combustion.
findings.wentWrong: Few could tell all four were gases; but-1-ene was named but-2-ene or propene; butane's structure was drawn badly; the combustion word equation defeated most.
findings.rule: Count carbons for the prefix (meth, eth, prop, but); draw every C-H bond; alkane + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water.

findings.asked: Fractional distillation processes, uses of fractions, then structures, names and reactions along the ethene-ethanol-ethanoic acid route.
findings.wentWrong: The steps of fractional distillation were not known even with a word list; the physical state of propane and the names ethanol and propanoic acid were often wrong.
findings.rule: Fractional distillation: crude oil heated and vaporised, column cooler at the top, fractions condense at their boiling points.

ruleToRemember: A homologous series has the same general formula, the same functional group, similar reactions and a gradual change in physical properties. Alkanes CnH2n+2, alkenes CnH2n, alcohols CnH2n+1OH; name by carbon count; a hydrocarbon is hydrogen and carbon only; complete combustion gives CO2 and H2O.
aStarSignal: Moving between name, molecular formula and full structural formula for any member of the series, and writing a balanced equation for incomplete combustion.
